name: ENCORE
description: "A control amplifier designed with an emphasis on phono circuits.It inherits the equalizer stage developed in the Audio Suite.The circuit can be switched in three stages from gain 36 dB to gain 60 dB. It is also compatible with low-power MC cartridges. In addition, three combinations of input impedance and load capacity can be selected.It is equipped with a Route 6 line input system and two tape input / output systems.The line input is also equipped with a single balanced input through a Fisher terminal. This balanced circuit can be used for devices with a balanced output. The gain can be switched in three stages from 0 dB to + 16 dB to be useful when low-power devices are connected.Outputs are provided in the Route 3. Two of the outputs are unbalanced via pin plugs, and the remaining one is balanced via Fischer plugs. These three outputs are connected in parallel and can be used to supply signals to multiple power amplifiers or to connect various processors.The tape output is equipped with a dedicated buffer amplifier that reduces the influence of the connected tape deck on the amplifier and ensures stable tone.For absolute phase switching, it is possible to perform fine polarity switching such as L side only and R side only, instead of simply switching 180 degrees polarity at L/R simultaneously.For the L/R balance adjustment, the gain is switched by changing the NF value of the amplifier itself.It is equipped with a mode switch, which tends to be omitted, with an emphasis on home music playback applications.The mode switch is in 5-position full mode.The volume control is equipped with a real 1 db step attenuator.The flat amplifier uses a large power transistor that supplies a large current to reduce the impedance of the circuit, ensuring stable operation in connection with various devices and complex music signals.The power supply unit is designed separately from the chassis."

name: ENCORE1MOHML
description: "This is a control amplifier that has been polished based on the Encore 1M � preamplifier and upgraded as a line input dedicated unit.It inherits the design philosophy of Encore 1M ¥, and is equipped with an input buffer amplifier with input impedance 1,000,000 � = 1M � from the viewpoint that it is ideal to have infinite input impedance. This makes it possible to play the program without losing the taste of the program source which cannot be obtained with other amplifiers by having input impedance which can be said to be practically infinite.In 1M � L, the line input regeneration is upgraded by the line input exclusive design, and the circuit is completely renewed.In particular, balanced transmission balance amplification is emphasized, and all circuits are configured with two independent amplifiers for the plus side and the minus side of the signal to achieve full balance amplification.The gain of the flat amplifier, which used to be 25 dB at the maximum, is reduced to 20 dB, and a larger input voltage ensures a larger dynamic range.Accordingly, the L/R-independent dB gain, which can also be used as a channel balancer, has been changed to a 1 db step variable between + 10 db and + 20 db.The volume section uses an ultra-precision attenuator that switches the fixed resistance in 1 dB steps (+ 10 ~ -40dB, -40 ~ -50dB in 2 dB steps).The attenuator was previously limited to -50dB steps, but now has 5 dB steps of -50 to -60dB to improve usability.Each circuit is a plug-in a module type, is a plug-in type card, which improves reliability and realizes low impedance by the thick power supply bar.The switch on the board enables floating / direct connection / disconnection between the audio ground and chassis ground at 10 ¥, making it possible to play with excellent SN ratio in combination with any power amplifier.There was a separately sold RMC phono equalizer for phono playback.The rear panel of the Encore 1M � L has a dedicated power terminal, and you can also play the phono by adding an RMC."

name: PERFORMANCE
description: "A monaural power amplifier with a fully monaural design.The Performance is designed with a separate large power supply and the Stereo is designed with a total of four chassis for a complete monaural design.The circuit configuration is pure A class operation up to 60W and AB class operation up to 390W.The amplifier circuit uses the same balanced circuitry as the Audio Suite and Audio Palette. The output stage uses a total of 44 output transistors for one channel only, 22 for the plus side and 22 for the minus side. Inside, these 22 transistors are housed in two cylindrical heat sinks, which are cooled by fans from the sides.The power supply uses a choke input with a choke coil with a large current capacity, and the transformer uses an EI-type core.The internal structure is a 2-layer structure with a driver stage and an output stage at the upper part, and an output stage with the same structure at the lower part.The chassis also contains sensors to protect against DC offset, abnormal heat generation, and excessive input.The AMATI speaker system in the cello can be connected directly by connecting four speaker outputs in parallel to allow for more than a by-wire connection.A barrier terminal is used to connect the power supply and amplifier.Direct 4.5mmx8 high-purity copper wire is used for the connecting cable to reduce sound quality degradation and energy loss.The input terminal is a balanced type, but unbalanced connection is also possible.A Fisher 3P connector is used for the balance input and bridge input."

name: RHAPSODY
description: "A 2-channel / 3-channel power amplifier developed as the first product of the new cello inherited by Matthew James.There were 2 types of variations, 2 channel configuration and 3 channel configuration.J-FET dual mono configuration is used for the input stage.This circuit has a wide dynamic range and is designed to be robust against overloads. This problem has been solved after careful consideration of voltage, current and frequency.In the driver stage and output stage, distortion is minimized even at a small signal level, and distortion components under actual operating conditions are minimized as much as possible.The output stage achieves stable operation by minimizing the amount of NF and making the circuit configuration simple.Six pairs of 250W metal-case bipolar transistors are used for each channel.The position on the semiconductor and heat sink and the choice of the heat sink itself are determined through trial and error in order to eliminate the effect of temperature change.The power transistors are mounted on metal hardware, compression washers, and a composite graphite-metal gasket that provides excellent thermal conductivity and is designed to maximize the performance of each device.Consideration is also given to the placement of the power transformer to minimize the influence of the transformer on other parts.A thick nickel-plated copper bus bar is used in some cases to more efficiently distribute power between the ground and the amplifier.The output signal from the amplifier is input to the bus bar through a 10 AWG gauge silver wire using capton as insulation.The power supply section uses a special high-temperature filter capacitor with a high-current terminal.Equipped with a microprocessor protection circuit.This processor protects the amplifier from speaker cable shorts, overheating, DC and overvoltages, as well as soft start, mute and analysis capabilities.The chassis is machined out of aircraft-grade hard aluminum.The legs are made of hardened stainless steel and are treated with an Almoloy coating to further increase the hardness through a low-temperature multi-state process. This reduces the cross-modulation distortion that occurs when the amplifier vibrates over a wide range and is effective even at 0.5 Hz. In addition, the mounting position is also taken into consideration to prevent the slight floor vibration from affecting the amplifier.XLR connector is used for input terminal.Remote trigger terminal is mounted."

name: R-DAC
description: "A reference D/A converter that inherits cello's unique sense of music beauty.Unlike conventional high-end D/A converters, the R-DAC does not require sound quality standards for analog disks or analog master tapes. Instead, the R-DAC refines sound quality by using raw performance sound before recording as a standard.In order to achieve this, we record the performance of a musician with a cello recording system and immediately play it back with an R-DAC to compare it with the live sound of the musician and improve the sound quality. We perform ideal sound quality tuning by evaluating the sound quality under exactly the same conditions, such as the recording technology, the physical characteristics of the room, and the psychological and mental condition of the engineer himself.The digital filter uses an 8 x oversampling method.An anti-imaging filter is used in the filter circuit to avoid roll-off and phase distortion at high frequencies usually caused by digital filters.Full 20-bit resolution provides high-quality playback over the entire bandwidth.The analog circuit uses P301, a premium output module that is also incorporated in the cello audio suite preamp.This module is a discrete configuration that eliminates circuit interference. It uses two modules per channel, so that it is guided to the output with the same phase management as a dual amplifier.The analog output gain can be adjusted with the trim pot on the rear panel, and the left / right balance can be adjusted with the built-in test tone.It is compatible with UV-22 (TM REG) Super CD encoding system developed by Apogee Electronics.This system enriches the information content of the low-level music signal even when playing CDs in the 16-bit normal format, and enables the transmission of delicate nuances.Equipped with Route 6 digital input, it can be connected to various devices.There are four AES/EBU inputs using the XLR terminal and two SPDIF inputs using the RCA terminal, both of which are gold-plated.The outputs have a Route 3 that can be used simultaneously.The balanced connector and XLR are gold-plated, and the unbalanced connector and RCA are gold-plated."
